segments.title: Boundary first
segments.screen: topology defense title and claim banner
segments.action: Point to FIXTURE / REDACTED / NOT LIVE before discussing the system.
say: This rehearsal demonstrates repeatability, observability, and recovery of the control plane.
This fixture run does not load a model, so it is not a real-model or physical dual-host performance claim; separate functional acceptance evidence remains distinct.

fallback.action: Copy the reported loopback URL into Edge; if Vite is unavailable, open the canonical snapshot source.

segments.title: One reproducible entrance
segments.screen: fixture banner, scenario manifest, and startup report
segments.action: Explain the single launcher, fixed routes, marker verification, two-minute startup budget, and owned-process cleanup.
say: One command starts only the current CyberGothic frontend and validates three fixed scenarios before declaring readiness.
Reports retain state and markers but omit credentials, model output, absolute paths, and dynamic ports.

fallback.action: Read the fail-closed report, state that this run is unavailable, and continue with tracked source and test evidence.

segments.title: Redacted topology and readiness
segments.screen: readiness checks, alias-only nodes, and layer segments
segments.action: Trace node-master to node-worker-a, then point out the excluded standby and complete L0-L23 projection.
say: The snapshot has three passing readiness checks, two ready aliases, and one offline standby excluded from allocation.
The stored end-exclusive ranges 0-8 and 8-24 render as L0-L7 and L8-L23 without a gap or overlap.

fallback.trigger: canvas or styles did not render
fallback.action: Use the accessible DOM text or canonical JSON; do not infer live topology from the decorative canvas.

segments.title: Failure is observable and recoverable
segments.screen: redacted failure report workflow and attempts
segments.action: Follow worker-ready, worker-exit, stage-reassigned, workflow-complete and compare lease epochs 1 and 2.
say: A real second worker process accepts the fixture stage and exits with code 23; the production transport observes remote_worker_disconnected.
The safe pure stage expires once, is reassigned exactly once to deterministic local recovery, and completes with its output redacted.

fallback.trigger: live failure injection did not finish
fallback.action: Say that the current replay failed, show the last redacted report only if present, and fall back to the deterministic regression test.

segments.title: Measure without overclaiming
segments.screen: performance closeout table and benchmark SVG claim banner
segments.action: Name the fixed workload first, read median and p95 second, and finish on the physical-dual-host not-run field.
say: Twelve measured and two warm-up iterations compare in-process with a real loopback worker process on one host.
These milliseconds measure TaskGraph control-plane fixture overhead, not TTFT, tokens per second, model quality, or dual-host acceleration.
success_markers: FIXTURE · SINGLE HOST · NOT MODEL PERFORMANCE

fallback.trigger: chart or fresh benchmark is unavailable
fallback.action: Show the JSON claim_guard; omit all measurements if no current report exists.

segments.title: Close on evidence and the next gate
segments.action: Summarize reproducibility, visible boundaries, deterministic recovery, the closed real-model functional gates, and the remaining performance boundary.
say: The result is a repeatable defense path with explicit evidence for startup, topology, recovery, and measurement.
Real runtime and model-switch functional acceptance are closed by separate GGUF evidence; this fixture still makes no model-performance or physical dual-host claim.
